discussion_comments.comment_body: AI Review: Opening Review records both a category and storage scope, but this clears only the storage when the session or project changes. The category remains active, so rendering and migration call `getMigrationCandidates(category, undefined)` and include candidates from every storage; newly discovered files are selected by default. Clear the category and return to the dashboard, or preserve and revalidate the category and storage together.

The picker now clears its Dev Container availability cache on each fresh open, so settings, configuration files, and Docker availability are rechecked. Forced in-place refreshes retain the current promise/result to avoid an async refresh loop. Added a regression test covering availability changing between opens.

**A stale `true` stays in place when a plugin drops out of a report.** This loop only updates identities present in the new report. Identities that were in `previous` but are missing now keep their value in `_runtimeEnablement` and in the model default. Together with the host filtering out `installed === false` (`copilotRuntimePluginEnablement.ts`), this means revoking a team assignment leaves the plugin shown as enabled, and forwarded to the host as Global `enabled: true`, until the window reloads.

Suggestion: for identities in `previous` but not in `report`, delete them from `_runtimeEnablement` and restore the persisted `installedPlugin.enabled` default, which means keeping that value next to `_discoveredPluginKeys`. A test for "plugin removed from report" would cover it.
What is the cache invalidation strategy? What happens if the allow list values changes in the server? Why are we caching only allow list values of a repo if we are fetching for all repos?

We cache per repo - this way if you change workspace and there are same repos, we will have the cache ready. Since it's per repo, we can construct various combinations of repos without having to hit the API.

There is background refresh instead of invalidation - i.e. we update from policy every 30 minutes. We should probably consider a force refresh mechanism as well.

AI Review: The ignore-case cache key folds pattern casing while cached `patterns` metadata retains the first spelling. If `glob.parse('**/bar', { ignoreCase: true })` warms the cache before parsing `{ '**/BAR': true, '**/BAZ': true }`, matching `BaR` now returns `**/bar`, which is not a key in the current expression. Please preserve current-expression spelling on cache hits or stop folding result-bearing cache keys, and add this cache-poisoning regression case.

Good point. Reduced the negative cache window to 6 hours in cea64934ad2 — that means a freshly-provisioned registry will be picked up within at most one working-day-length cycle, while still skipping the 1–2s startup hit on the typical relaunch-after-an-hour case that motivated this change. A non-blocking background refresh would be a nicer fix but is more invasive than I want to do in this PR; happy to follow up with that separately if the shorter window is still considered too long.

This service seems to be doing too much. It should use marketplace account service and ask for a vlaid account it can use for private marketplace. All access / entitlement checks should be done by the marketplace account service. Also there should be an event on the account service when account has changed.

AI Review: Returning `undefined` is committed by `InlineCompletionsSource` as an empty state whose request can satisfy later fetches at the same model version and position. Because connection state is not part of the cache key and this provider does not react to metered-state changes, switching back to unmetered can leave completions absent until an edit. Please invalidate or bypass the cached request and trigger a fresh automatic fetch on the metered-to-unmetered transition, with model-level coverage.

Fixed in 1af83fb27fd. Default non-aware providers now publish a provider-change signal when the connection becomes unmetered. Provider-triggered fetches carry `forceUpdate`, so `InlineCompletionsSource` bypasses both an in-flight/cache-satisfying request and the committed empty state without requiring a model edit. The model tests now fire provider changes at the same position and cover both provider-change branches.
